one_liner: Executive who runs the SEC Division of Examinations' risk-analytics and monitoring office, setting risk-based exam strategy for broker-dealers, investment advisers and other registrants.
fit_summary: This is a senior executive-level SEC role that requires a full year of GS-14-equivalent experience examining or overseeing securities firms. Nothing on file shows securities-industry, audit or financial-regulatory experience. Daniel's emergency-management consulting and policy knowledge do not match this specialized experience, so an application would very likely be screened out at minimum qualifications.
eligibility: Open to the public, so U.S. citizens without federal status may apply.

Requires at least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-14/SK-14: examining, auditing or reviewing broker-dealers, investment advisers, investment companies, transfer agents or SROs, or managing teams that do so.
Requires a Top Secret security clearance; confirm whether you must already hold it or can be investigated after selection.
Must be in one of the listed SEC offices, with Washington, DC the nearest to Manassas; telework is not available.
strategy: Be honest with yourself about the securities-examination requirement. Without documented experience examining or assessing registered securities firms, you are better off skipping this posting than spending effort on it.

If you apply anyway, frame any IEM work only where it is truly accurate, for example risk assessment, incident response coordination or governance support for government clients. Do not imply securities-regulatory experience you do not have.

Use the posting's dates (October 23 to November 6, 2026) as a benchmark, and redirect your energy to emergency-management and policy roles at GS-9 to GS-12. Good targets are FEMA, DHS, Virginia VDEM, and Prince William County or City of Manassas emergency management.
For any federal application, keep the resume to two pages. List dates, hours per week and specialized experience concisely, using the posting's exact wording.

Note this posting's process for future senior roles: there is no Accomplishment Record at application, but if you are found qualified you get only 3 business days to submit 300-word narratives. Draft STAR examples in advance.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] during [disaster/recovery program] at IEM by [coordinating/analyzing/briefing] [specific task], resulting in [verifiable outcome].
Built working relationships with [number/type of stakeholders, e.g., state and local officials] to share information and resolve [issue] during [project], as [your title], [hours] hrs/week, [dates].
Assessed [type of risk or program data] for [client] and presented findings to [audience], informing [decision or plan].
interview_questions: Describe a time you led a team conducting examinations or reviews of securities firms. How did you set priorities based on risk?
How would you integrate risk analytics into national exam planning across program areas?
Tell us about building a coalition with external regulators or SROs during a significant market event.
How have you aligned limited resources with competing organizational priorities?
watch_outs: The specialized experience requirement for securities examination or oversight at the GS-14 level is almost certainly unmet, so you would likely be rated ineligible.
A Top Secret clearance is required.
The job is on-site only, with no telework, which would mean a daily commute to the DC office.
If you are found qualified, you have only 3 business days to submit the Accomplishment Record.
